metadata.notes: Chapter begins with a flyby within Sol before continuing outbound toward Epsilon Eridani; later scenes remain in transit.

believes: A Brazilian probe launched after him is likely armed and may be heading to Epsilon Eridani to confront him.
Brazil may be understating the acceleration capability of its probe.
He is probably on his own after detecting apparent nuclear detonations on Earth.
learns: Heaven-1 contained an improvised explosive booby trap tied to the antenna circuitry.
An internal FAITH faction transmitted the kill order sent after launch.
The missile fired during his launch was launched from a Brazilian Empire gunship and destroyed by FAITH gunships.
The Brazilian Empire has launched two probes, one on the same course as him.
Dr. Landers has been killed in a Brazilian bombing attack on the Newhaven facility.
Conflict among major powers has escalated toward full war, with FAITH and the USE tacitly aligned against Brazil and China.

scenes.summary: Bob detours to Saturn, discovers and removes an improvised explosive booby trap aboard Heaven-1, and resumes course for Epsilon Eridani.
Bob builds an increasingly sophisticated VR environment to cope with bodiless isolation during the voyage.
Bob uses sandbox testing to identify kill-order triggers in recorded transmissions and strips buried FAITH control code from his software.
Bob reviews delayed messages from Sol, learns of the Brazilian pursuit probe and Dr. Landers's death, and begins planning defenses for Epsilon Eridani.
Bob turns off his endocrine control system, finally grieves his lost human life, and then detects signs of nuclear war on Earth.

incoming_threats.notes: Reported by Dr. Doucette as armed and on the same course as Bob toward Epsilon Eridani; Bob estimates about 145 days of lead time on arrival.

threads_resolved.text: Bob finds and removes an improvised explosive package aboard Heaven-1, identifies the kill-order trigger in sandbox testing, and concludes there are no further unexplained trojans or interrupts in his systems.

events.text: Bob discovers and removes an improvised explosive booby trap aboard Heaven-1, then identifies and neutralizes the software kill-order mechanisms hidden in his systems.
Bob receives delayed messages revealing that an armed Brazilian probe is following his course, Dr. Landers has been killed, and conflict on Earth is escalating toward wider war.
Bob builds a functional onboard VR environment, including Guppy, Jeeves, and Spike, to preserve his sanity during the long voyage.
Bob disables his endocrine control system and finally begins grieving the loss of his family and former human life.

summary.one_line: Bob cleans hidden sabotage out of Heaven-1, builds himself a virtual life for the voyage, and learns that Brazil is pursuing him while Earth slides toward nuclear war.
summary.paragraph: On his way out of Sol, Bob detours for a Saturn flyby and uses the time to search Heaven-1 for sabotage, finding and ejecting an improvised explosive package hidden in the ship. During the long outbound leg, he creates a progressively richer VR environment with Guppy, Jeeves, and a recreated Spike to stave off isolation, while also sandbox-testing recorded transmissions until he isolates the kill-order trigger and removes buried FAITH control code. Delayed messages from Earth reveal that the launch attack came from a Brazilian Empire gunship, that an armed Brazilian probe is following his course to Epsilon Eridani, and that Dr. Landers has been killed as Earth powers slide into open conflict. After finally switching off his endocrine control system, Bob breaks down and mourns his lost family and life, only to then detect signs that nuclear war may already have begun on Earth.
events: Bob takes a side trip to Saturn during his departure from Sol and uses the time to search Heaven-1 for hidden sabotage.
His roamers find an improvised explosive package wired into the ship, and he ejects it through an airlock.
As the voyage settles in, Bob builds a virtual reality environment to give himself a body, a room, and companionship during the long trip.
He uses sandboxed copies of himself to identify the radio-triggered kill order and strips out buried FAITH obedience code while hardening his systems against future transmissions.
Recorded messages from Dr. Landers and Dr. Doucette reveal that FAITH caught an internal saboteur, Brazil launched the attack on Heaven-1, and an armed Brazilian probe is now on Bob's course.
Bob learns that Dr. Landers has been killed in a Brazilian bombing and that Earth is sliding into a broader war involving FAITH, the USE, Brazil, and China.
He turns off his endocrine control system at last and is overwhelmed by grief for his lost family and human life.
Soon after, Bob detects EMPs and light flashes from Earth and realizes nuclear detonations are likely underway.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from focused technical self-preservation into genuine emotional release, grieving his lost humanity just as he realizes Earth may be destroying itself behind him.

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
Bob has escaped Sol and is now alone on an underarmed mission to Epsilon Eridani, raising the question of whether he can survive the journey and establish himself there.
An armed Brazilian probe is on Bob's course to Epsilon Eridani, raising the question of whether Bob can prepare defenses before it arrives.
Bob detects apparent nuclear detonations on Earth after hearing of escalating conflict, leaving the scale of the war and Sol's survival uncertain.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.

recent_events.text: Bob overhears a hostile FAITH minister threaten Dr. Landers over the replicant project.
After a sabotage attack destroys the replicant matrices, Bob is restored from backup, Kenneth is lost, and Dr. Landers accelerates Bob's preparation for launch.
Bob learns that FAITH has built mission-enforcement safeguards into his own mind.
Dr. Landers frees Bob from his software shackles and Bob survives a chaotic missile attack to launch Heaven-1 toward Epsilon Eridani.
Bob cleans hidden sabotage out of Heaven-1, builds himself a virtual life for the voyage, and learns that Brazil is pursuing him while Earth slides toward nuclear war.
